newsitem.title: USA: Wash. 1,158 MW nuclear unit reducing to 25 pct.
newsitem.headline: Wash. 1,158 MW nuclear unit reducing to 25 pct.

text.p: The 1,158 megawatt (MW) WNP-2 nuclear unit at Richland, Wash., will be reduced to 25 percent power through Friday before beginning to power back up, a spokesman for the plant said Thursday.

The unit has been operating at between 58 to 68 percent capacity since mid-January due to problems with an adjustable speed drive, and needs to be brought down further before restarting the pump linked to the drive, the spokesman said.
The unit will start reducing power mid-morning Thursday, reach 25 percent Thursday evening before beginning to ascend back up to 85 percent capacity by Friday evening.
The plant will then be brought down to 70 percent for the weekend at the request of Bonneville Power Administration (BPA), which markets power produced from the nuclear unit.
"They still have a lot of water and hydropower," the WNP-2 spokesman said.
He was not sure what rate the plant would operate at after 0600 PST on Monday.
